title: Issue is common-consent dogma — not whether some Reformed gave occasion for the charge
source_text: CXXX. Ubi diligenter observatum velim inter me & virum Doctum quaestionem non esse, An quidam ex Reformatis occasionem dederint ista ipsis imputandi? Nec enim Thesis asserit ista non posse absque calumnia ullis ex Doctoribus Reformatis tribui. Sed hoc quaeri, An Scholae Reformatae Theologi ista communi consensu doceant, tanquam fidei inter ipsos receptae dogmata atque articulos, quibus subscribant omnes hactenus noti & alicujus nominis Reformati, exceptis solum duobus vel tribus novis hominibus? quod affirmat vir Doctus. Et quod in Thesi asserui, & de novo constanter assero, non posse absque calumnia poni & affirmari. Itaque ad Thesis meae defensionem suffecerit, si manifeste ostendam multos ex Reformatis veteribus & recentioribus, qui scriptis suis sunt apud suos celebres, & in Schola Reformata pro viris piis & Orthodoxis habentur, quae nobis imputat vir Doctus rejicere & repudiare. Contra vero nihil egerit vir Doctus, etiamsi proferre posset aliquot ex Reformatis, qui, vel ista docuerint, vel saltem ea scripserint ex quibus videntur aperte deduci; dummodo sint qui contrariam asserant, & aliud hac in parte se sentire profitantur, nec propterea tamen pro Heterodoxis a suis habeantur.
pass_a_gloss: Where I would have it carefully observed that the question between me and the Learned Man is not whether certain of the Reformed have given occasion for those things to be imputed to them. For the Thesis does not assert that those things cannot without calumny be attributed to any of the Reformed Doctors. But this is asked: whether the Theologians of the Reformed School teach those things by common consent, as dogmas and articles of faith received among them, to which all Reformed hitherto known and of any name subscribe, except only two or three new men? — which the Learned Man affirms. And what I asserted in the Thesis, and freshly constantly assert, cannot without calumny be laid down and affirmed. Therefore for defense of my Thesis it will suffice if I clearly show that many of the older and more recent Reformed who are celebrated among their own by their writings, and are held in the Reformed School for pious and Orthodox men, reject and repudiate what the Learned Man imputes to us. Conversely the Learned Man will have accomplished nothing even if he could produce some of the Reformed who either taught those things or at least wrote things from which they seem openly deduced — provided there are those who assert the contrary and profess to sense otherwise on this point, and are not on that account held Heterodox by their own.
pass_b_english: The real question is not whether some Reformed gave occasion for the charge.
It is whether Reformed theologians teach those four points by common consent as received faith-articles nearly all subscribe — as the opponent claims. Le Blanc says affirming that is calumny.

Defense needs only many celebrated Orthodox Reformed who reject the imputation; a few who taught or seemed to imply it does not prove school-wide dogma while others contradict without being branded heterodox.
